Can you explain auto trim?
intent_routes.answer: Auto trim controls how aggressively the autopilot applies rudder to compensate for constant heading offset caused by external forces like wind or current. Lower auto trim provides faster limitation of constant heading offset.

intent_routes.question: What is the rudder limit setting?
question_variations: How does rudder limit work?
What does rudder limit control?
What is maximum rudder movement?
intent_routes.answer: Rudder limit determines the maximum rudder movement in degrees from midship position that autopilot can command in automatic modes. It only applies during autosteering on straight courses, not during course changes or Follow-up/Non-Follow-up steering.

intent_routes.question: What triggers an autopilot alarm?
question_variations: When does the autopilot alarm go off?
What causes the autopilot to alarm?
How much deviation triggers an autopilot alarm?
intent_routes.answer: An alarm occurs when the actual heading deviates from the set heading more than the selected limit.

intent_routes.question: What is track response in autopilot settings?
question_variations: How does track response work?
What does the track response setting do?
Can you explain track response?
intent_routes.answer: Track response defines how fast the autopilot responds after having registered a cross track distance.

intent_routes.question: What is the track approach angle setting?
question_variations: How does track approach angle work?
What does track approach angle control?
intent_routes.answer: Track approach angle defines the angle used when the vessel is approaching a leg. This setting is used both when starting navigation and when using track offset.

intent_routes.question: How do I use dual radar?
question_variations: Can I use two radars at once?
Is it possible to show two radar sources?
intent_routes.answer: You can use a dual panel page to show radar images from two different radar sources. However, interference may occur when using Broadband Radar with pulse or Halo radar simultaneously. It's recommended to only transmit on one radar at a time.

intent_routes.question: How do I select a radar source?
question_variations: Where do I choose which radar to use?
How can I switch between radar sources?
intent_routes.answer: Specify the radar in the radar panel by selecting from available radars in the radar source menu option. For multiple radar panels, activate each panel individually and select different radar sources. The 3-digit radar source number corresponds to the last 3 digits of the radar's serial number.

intent_routes.question: What is radar overlay?
question_variations: How does radar overlay work?
Can I overlay radar on charts?
intent_routes.answer: Radar overlay allows you to overlay the Radar image on the Chart, helping interpret radar images by correlating radar targets with charted objects. A heading sensor must be present in the system for radar overlay to work.

intent_routes.question: How do I enable radar overlay on the chart?
question_variations: How to turn on radar overlay?
Can I show radar on my chart display?
How do I activate radar overlay?
intent_routes.answer: A heading sensor must be present in the system to use radar overlay. Select radar overlay from the Chart panel menu, then use Radar options and Source to select the radar source.

intent_routes.question: What are the main radar operational modes?
question_variations: What modes can the radar operate in?
How many radar modes are there?
What are the different radar states?
intent_routes.answer: There are four main radar operational modes: Power Off (scanner powered down), Standby (power on but not transmitting), Transmit (scanner on and transmitting), and Power Save (available on Halo20+ and Halo24 only).

intent_routes.question: How does Power Save mode work on radar?
question_variations: What is radar power save mode?
How does radar power saving function?
Can I set power save on my radar?
intent_routes.answer: Power Save mode alternates between transmit and standby periods. Default settings are 20 scans during transmit followed by 3 minutes standby. During standby, the radar image freezes and becomes grey-scaled. This cycle continues until changed to another mode.

intent_routes.question: Where do I adjust radar range?
question_variations: How to change radar range?
Can I zoom the radar display?
How do I modify radar distance?
intent_routes.answer: Radar range can be adjusted by selecting the zoom icons on the radar panel.

intent_routes.question: What happens to Guard Zone alarms in Power Save mode?
question_variations: Do guard zones work in power save?
Are alarms active during power save?
Will radar alerts work in power save mode?
intent_routes.answer: Guard Zone alarms remain active during power save mode. If an alarm triggers, the radar will exit power save and remain transmitting indefinitely until power save is manually re-enabled.

intent_routes.question: How do I adjust the radar range?
question_variations: Where are the radar range controls?
Can I change the radar range?
How do I zoom the radar in and out?
intent_routes.answer: Adjust radar range by selecting the zoom icons on the radar panel

intent_routes.question: What is dual range mode?
question_variations: Can I use dual range?
How does dual range work?
Is dual range available on my radar?
intent_routes.answer: Dual range mode allows radar to run as two virtual radar sources A and B with independent range and controls. Available on Broadband 4G and Halo radar models except Halo20

intent_routes.question: What is sector blanking?
question_variations: How does sector blanking work?
Can I blank out radar sectors?
Which radars support sector blanking?
intent_routes.answer: Sector blanking stops radar transmission in up to 4 sectors to prevent interference from masts or structures. Only available on Halo radars and configured in radar installation dialog

intent_routes.question: What radar modes are available?
question_variations: What are the different radar modes?
Which radar modes can I use?
How many radar modes are there?
intent_routes.answer: Available modes include Custom, Harbor, Offshore, Weather, Bird modes. Not all modes available on all radar models

intent_routes.question: What are the Harbor mode settings?
question_variations: How does Harbor mode work?
What settings are used in Harbor mode?
When should I use Harbor mode?
intent_routes.answer: Harbor mode optimizes for busy waterways and structures with high noise rejection, low target expansion, fast scan off, and SC/SC-3 scan to scan settings

intent_routes.question: How do I adjust sea clutter settings on the radar?
question_variations: What are the sea clutter options?
How can I reduce sea clutter?
intent_routes.answer: The system has predefined sea clutter settings for harbor and offshore conditions, plus a manual mode. In Auto mode, you can fine-tune using Auto Sea Offset. Adjust according to current sea conditions for best clutter rejection.

intent_routes.question: What does the radar gain control do?
question_variations: How does gain affect radar sensitivity?
What happens if radar gain is too high?
intent_routes.answer: Gain controls radar receiver sensitivity. Higher gain displays weaker targets but may cause background noise clutter. It has manual and automatic modes, toggled via slide bar or by pressing/holding the rotary knob.

intent_routes.question: How do I reduce rain interference on radar?
question_variations: What is rain clutter adjustment?
How to filter out rain on radar?
intent_routes.answer: Use Rain Clutter to reduce effects of rain, snow or weather. Increasing the value reduces long-distance clutter from rain. Don't increase too much as it may filter real targets. Near ship precipitation affects nearby echo presentation.

intent_routes.question: How does the cursor assist function work?
question_variations: What is radar cursor assist?
How do I use cursor assist?
intent_routes.answer: Press and hold finger on screen to change cursor to selection circle above finger. Drag circle to desired position while keeping finger on screen. Cursor returns to normal when finger is removed.

intent_routes.question: What is the radar threshold setting?
question_variations: How does threshold affect radar display?
What does radar threshold control?
intent_routes.answer: Threshold sets required signal strength for lowest radar signals. Returns below this limit are filtered and not displayed. Default is 30% for less clutter.

intent_routes.question: What is target expansion in radar?
question_variations: How does target expansion work?
What does the target expansion feature do?
Can you explain radar target expansion?
intent_routes.answer: Target expansion increases the length of targets in range, making them easier to see on the radar display.

intent_routes.question: How does interference rejection work?
question_variations: What is IR in radar?
When should I use interference rejection?
How do I handle radar interference?
intent_routes.answer: Interference rejection (IR) eliminates second trace echoes and interference from other radar units by changing the transceiver PRF slightly for each sweep. Use IR ON when interference exists, OFF when maximum signal is needed or when no interference exists.

intent_routes.question: What is VelocityTrack in radar?
question_variations: How does VelocityTrack work?
What does VelocityTrack do?
Can you explain radar VelocityTrack?
intent_routes.answer: VelocityTrack is a navigation aid that uses Doppler coloring to distinguish moving targets approaching or diverging from your vessel. It works when the target's relative speed exceeds the threshold and the target is not stationary.

intent_routes.question: What colors are used for approaching targets in radar?
question_variations: How are approaching targets colored?
What color indicates approaching vessels?
How do I identify approaching targets by color?
intent_routes.answer: Approaching target colors vary by palette: Yellow on Black/Red and White/Red palettes, Red on Black/Green and Black/Yellow palettes. On chart overlays, approaching targets are yellow and diverging targets are dark grey.

intent_routes.question: How does Fast Scan work?
question_variations: What is Fast Scan mode?
How do I get faster target updates?
What does Fast Scan do?
intent_routes.answer: Fast Scan increases the speed of radar antenna rotation to provide faster target updates. Maximum speed depends on radar Settings, Mode, and Range selected, as the radar will only rotate as fast as current control settings allow.

intent_routes.question: What is Harbor Mode in radar?
question_variations: What does Harbor Mode do?
How does Harbor Mode work?
What are Harbor Mode settings?
intent_routes.answer: Harbor Mode optimizes radar settings for busy waterways and large man-made structures where good target discrimination and rapid image updates are needed. It uses High noise rejection, Low target expansion, Fast scan mode Off, and SC/SC-3 scan-to-scan settings.

intent_routes.question: What is Offshore Mode in radar?
question_variations: How does Offshore Mode work?
What are the Offshore Mode settings?
When should I use Offshore Mode?
intent_routes.answer: Offshore Mode optimizes radar settings for offshore sea conditions and makes isolated targets larger and easier to see. It uses High noise rejection, Medium target expansion, Fast scan mode Off, and SC/SC-2 scan-to-scan settings.

intent_routes.question: How does Dual Range mode work?
question_variations: Can I use different modes in dual range?
What are the limitations of dual range mode?
How do dual range settings interact?
intent_routes.answer: In Dual Range mode, you can set different modes for each range (e.g., Offshore for range A and Weather for range B). However, some settings interact: Fast scan speed uses the slower of the two selected modes, and Interference reject settings affect both ranges.

intent_routes.question: What is Directional clutter rejection?
question_variations: How does Directional clutter rejection work?
When is Directional clutter rejection active?
Can I adjust Directional clutter rejection?
intent_routes.answer: Directional clutter rejection is active when Sea clutter is set to Auto or Harbor/Offshore. It dynamically adjusts radar receiver gain during 360-degree sweeps based on sea clutter levels, improving target sensitivity to leeward and in heavy seas. Halo radars allow fine-tuning via Auto offset adjustments.

intent_routes.question: How does Sea clutter filtering work?
question_variations: What does Sea clutter setting do?
How do I adjust Sea clutter?
What are the Sea clutter modes?
intent_routes.answer: Sea clutter filtering reduces random echo returns from waves or rough water near the vessel. Increasing the value reduces near-field clutter sensitivity, but too high values can make targets disappear. It includes predefined settings for harbor and offshore conditions, plus manual mode. Note that at high sea clutter levels, small objects like buoys may become undetectable.

intent_routes.question: How do I set true motion on the radar?
question_variations: How can I enable true motion display?
What are the steps to set true motion?
intent_routes.answer: Select the Position option in the More menu, then select the True motion option

intent_routes.question: What are target trails used for?
question_variations: Why should I use target trails?
What is the purpose of target trails?
intent_routes.answer: Target trails show target movement by leaving an afterglow that gradually fades, helping to quickly assess target movement relative to your vessel

intent_routes.question: How do I clear target trails?
question_variations: Can I remove target trails?
What's the way to delete target trails?
intent_routes.answer: Select the clear trails option to temporarily remove target trails from the radar panel. Trails will rebuild unless the function is switched off

intent_routes.question: How do I set up an EBL/VRM marker?
question_variations: What are the steps to create an EBL/VRM marker?
How can I place an EBL/VRM marker?
intent_routes.answer: 1. Ensure cursor is not active 2. Activate More menu 3. Select EBL/VRM 4. Choose EBL/VRM 1 or 2 5. Adjust position if needed 6. Save settings

intent_routes.question: How do I set up a guard zone?
question_variations: What are the steps to create a guard zone?
How can I create a radar guard zone?
intent_routes.answer: 1. Ensure cursor is not active 2. Activate menu and select Guard zones 3. Choose a guard zone 4. Select shape (circular or sector) 5. Adjust settings for bearing, depth, range, and width 6. Save settings

intent_routes.question: What does VelocityTrack color coding mean in radar?
question_variations: What do the different colors mean in VelocityTrack?
How do I interpret VelocityTrack colors?
What do red and blue targets mean on radar?
intent_routes.answer: Red indicates approaching targets with relative speed above threshold, blue indicates diverging targets above threshold, and no color (neutral) indicates targets with relative speed below the threshold

intent_routes.question: What are the available radar orientation modes?
question_variations: How can I change radar orientation?
What orientation settings does the radar have?
What do HU, NU, and CU mean in radar?
intent_routes.answer: Three orientation modes are available: Head-up (HU), North-up (NU), and Course-up (CU). These are displayed in the upper left corner of the radar panel

intent_routes.question: How does Head-up radar mode work?
question_variations: What is Head-up radar mode?
Can you explain HU radar orientation?
When is Head-up mode available?
intent_routes.answer: Head-up mode orients the heading line at 0° on the bearing scale toward screen top. The radar image displays relative to own ship and rotates when ship turns. It's only available in relative motion mode and when no heading source is connected

intent_routes.question: What happens in North-up radar mode?
question_variations: How does North-up mode work?
What is NU radar orientation?
Can you explain North-up radar display?
intent_routes.answer: In North-up mode, 0° on PPI represents north. Heading line orients to ship's heading from compass. When ship turns, heading line changes direction while radar image remains stable. Requires heading source connection

intent_routes.question: How does Course-up radar mode function?
question_variations: What is Course-up mode in radar?
How does CU radar orientation work?
What happens in Course-up display?
intent_routes.answer: In Course-up mode, bearing scale top indicates ship's true course from north when activated. During turns, bearing scale stays fixed while heading line rotates with ship's yawing and course changes. Mode must be reselected to reset

intent_routes.question: What is the difference between True Motion and Relative Motion on radar?
question_variations: How does True Motion differ from Relative Motion?
What are the radar motion modes?
Can you explain TM vs RM on radar?
intent_routes.answer: In Relative Motion (RM), your vessel remains fixed on the radar display while other objects move relative to your position. In True Motion (TM), your vessel and all moving targets move across the radar display while stationary objects remain fixed.

intent_routes.question: How do I offset the PPI center on radar?
question_variations: Can I change the radar antenna position?
What are the PPI center options?
How do I adjust radar center position?
intent_routes.answer: There are three options to offset the PPI center: 1) Center - resets antenna position to center of PPI, 2) Look Ahead - places PPI center at 70% radius opposite display top (only in heading up mode), 3) Offset - allows manual selection of PPI center using cursor.

intent_routes.question: When does True Motion reset occur?
question_variations: At what point does the radar image redraw in True Motion?
How far can the vessel symbol travel before True Motion resets?
intent_routes.answer: In True Motion, when the vessel symbol reaches 75% of the PPI radius, the radar image automatically redraws with the vessel symbol repositioned 180° opposite the current heading bearing.

intent_routes.question: How do I enable True Motion on my radar?
question_variations: What settings are needed for True Motion?
Can I switch to True Motion mode?
intent_routes.answer: To enable True Motion, the PPI must be in either north up or course up orientation mode. Select the Position option in the More menu, then select the True motion option on the MFD.

intent_routes.question: Where is the radar motion mode displayed?
question_variations: How can I tell if I'm in True Motion or Relative Motion?
Where do I see the current radar motion mode?
intent_routes.answer: The radar motion mode is indicated in the upper left corner of the radar panel as either TM (True motion) or RM (Relative motion).

intent_routes.question: What is the maximum range for tracking zones?
question_variations: How far can tracking zones reach?
What's the tracking zone distance limit?
What range do tracking zones cover?
intent_routes.answer: The maximum range for tracking zones is 42 nautical miles (NM)

intent_routes.question: How many targets can ZoneTrack monitor per zone?
question_variations: What's the target limit for ZoneTrack?
How many targets can each zone track?
What is the maximum number of tracked targets per zone?
intent_routes.answer: ZoneTrack has a limit of 50 targets per zone. This limit cannot be changed.

intent_routes.question: What's the difference between guard zones and target tracking zones?
question_variations: How do guard zones differ from tracking zones?
Are guard zones the same as target tracking zones?
What makes guard zones different from tracking zones?
intent_routes.answer: Guard zones only raise alarms when targets enter the zone but don't track automatically. Target tracking zones automatically acquire and track radar targets when they enter the zone.

intent_routes.question: How many guard zones can be defined?
question_variations: What's the maximum number of guard zones?
How many zones can I set up?
Can I have multiple guard zones?
intent_routes.answer: Two zones can be defined, each with individual settings

intent_routes.question: What happens when ZoneTrack is disabled?
question_variations: What occurs when I turn off ZoneTrack?
How does unselecting ZoneTrack affect tracking?
What are the effects of disabling ZoneTrack?
intent_routes.answer: When ZoneTrack is unselected, all zones are disabled and removed from the radar image. The radar stops acquiring targets inside the zones and no alarms will be sent.

intent_routes.question: What happens if a radar target goes behind an island?
question_variations: Does the system still track targets behind obstacles?
How does target tracking work with obstructions?
What happens to tracking when radar loses line of sight?
intent_routes.answer: The system continues tracking and visualizing the AIS target even if the radar target is positioned behind an island, using the association function to maintain tracking.

intent_routes.question: How are dangerous targets defined?
question_variations: What makes a target dangerous?
When is a vessel considered dangerous?
How does the system identify dangerous targets?
intent_routes.answer: Dangerous targets are defined in the Vessels and tracked targets dialog using TCPA/CPA settings. The Dangerous vessel option must be enabled in the Alarms settings dialog to receive alerts.

intent_routes.question: What options are available when a dangerous target is detected?
question_variations: How can I respond to a dangerous target alert?
What can I do when I get a dangerous vessel warning?
What are my options for dangerous target notifications?
intent_routes.answer: Three options are available: Disable (cancels alerts for all vessels), Ignore (disables alert for specific vessel), and View (shows vessel on radar panel with details popup).

intent_routes.question: How many MARPA targets can be tracked?
question_variations: What is the maximum number of MARPA targets?
How many radar targets can be tracked simultaneously?
What's the MARPA tracking limit?
intent_routes.answer: The MARPA function can track up to ten radar targets simultaneously when the system includes a heading sensor.

intent_routes.question: What happens when I select Disable for dangerous target alerts?
question_variations: How does the Disable option affect dangerous target warnings?
What occurs after disabling dangerous target alerts?
Will I still get alerts after hitting Disable?
intent_routes.answer: Selecting Disable turns off the Dangerous target alert option in the Alarms settings dialog and cancels dangerous target alerts for all vessels. No alert messages will be generated for either radar or AIS dangerous targets until re-enabled.

intent_routes.question: How do I set up a guard zone on the radar?
question_variations: What are the steps to create a guard zone?
How do I configure a radar guard zone?
What's the process for setting up radar zones?
intent_routes.answer: 1. Ensure cursor is not active 2. Activate menu and select guard zone 3. Select zone shape (sector or circle) 4. Select Adjust to define settings including bearing, depth, range and width. Settings can be adjusted via menu or by dragging on radar panel.

intent_routes.question: When does the guard zone alarm trigger?
question_variations: How do guard zone alarms work?
What triggers a guard zone alarm?
How can I set guard zone alerts?
intent_routes.answer: Guard zone alarms can be set to trigger either when a target enters or exits the zone. This is configured using the 'Alarm when' option in the settings.

intent_routes.question: How do I watch specific radar targets?
question_variations: What is the target watching feature?
Can I track particular radar targets?
How do I highlight specific targets?
intent_routes.answer: Select a target and choose the 'Watch target' option to highlight it. Multiple targets can be watched simultaneously. To stop watching, select the watched target and choose 'Stop watching' option.

intent_routes.question: What do the different radar target symbols mean?
question_variations: How do I interpret radar target icons?
What are the radar target indicators?
What do the radar symbols represent?
intent_routes.answer: Radar symbols include: stationary targets (no movement), moving targets with trails, moving targets with course extensions, and dangerous targets shown in yellow, purple, or red depending on the radar palette.

intent_routes.question: What is target association?
question_variations: How does radar and AIS target association work?
What happens when radar and AIS detect the same target?
How are combined radar and AIS targets displayed?
intent_routes.answer: Target association displays radar and AIS signals from the same target as a single symbol to reduce clutter. The system continues tracking both signals and can maintain tracking through AIS if radar contact is lost, such as when behind an island.

intent_routes.question: What is MARPA tracking used for?
question_variations: Why do we use MARPA tracking?
What's the purpose of MARPA tracking?
intent_routes.answer: MARPA tracking is an important tool for collision avoidance

intent_routes.question: How long does it take to acquire a MARPA target?
question_variations: What's the acquisition time for MARPA targets?
How many rotations to acquire MARPA?
intent_routes.answer: It typically takes up to 10 full rotations of the scanner to acquire a MARPA target

intent_routes.question: What indicates a dangerous MARPA target?
question_variations: How do I identify a dangerous MARPA target?
When is a MARPA target considered dangerous?
intent_routes.answer: A target is defined as dangerous when it enters the guard zone defined on the radar panel. It will be shown in yellow, purple, or red depending on the radar palette being used

intent_routes.question: What is a tracked associated MARPA target?
question_variations: How does MARPA target association work?
What happens when radar and AIS track the same target?
intent_routes.answer: When the radar and AIS signal acquire the same target for tracking, the system displays it as one symbol to reduce clutter. The association function continues tracking via AIS if radar tracking fails, such as when behind an island

intent_routes.question: What happens to lost MARPA targets?
question_variations: How does the system handle lost MARPA targets?
What's displayed when MARPA tracking is lost?
intent_routes.answer: When no signals have been received within a time limit, a target is defined as lost. The target symbol shows the last valid position before reception of data was lost

intent_routes.question: How do I track MARPA targets on radar?
question_variations: What are the steps to track MARPA targets?
How can I acquire MARPA targets?
What's the process for tracking radar targets?
intent_routes.answer: 1. Position cursor on target on radar image 2. Select Acquire targets from menu 3. Repeat for additional targets. Note: It may take up to 10 radar sweeps to acquire and track the target.

intent_routes.question: How do I cancel MARPA target tracking?
question_variations: Can I stop tracking a MARPA target?
What's the way to cancel radar target tracking?
intent_routes.answer: Select the target icon before activating the menu to cancel tracking of individual targets.

intent_routes.question: Where can I view MARPA target information?
question_variations: How do I see MARPA target details?
What displays MARPA target data?
intent_routes.answer: Target information can be viewed by: 1. Selecting target when pop-up is activated 2. Checking data bar for 3 closest targets 3. Using Vessels tool option on Home page for all targets

intent_routes.question: What MARPA alarms can be set?
question_variations: Which alarm settings are available for MARPA?
How do I configure MARPA alarms?
intent_routes.answer: Two main MARPA alarms can be set: 1. MARPA target lost alarm 2. MARPA unavailable alarm (triggers when required inputs are missing). Additionally, guard zone alarms can be set for when targets enter defined zones.

intent_routes.question: How do I record radar data?
question_variations: Can I save radar data?
What's the process for recording radar information?
intent_routes.answer: Radar data can be recorded internally or to a connected storage device. It's recommended to record directly to a microSD card due to data size. Recording must be enabled in Advanced system settings first.

intent_routes.question: How do I show or hide radar range rings?
question_variations: Can I display range rings on radar?
How to toggle radar rings?
Where are the range ring settings?
intent_routes.answer: Select 'Settings' then 'Radar' to show/hide range rings. You can specify the number of rings to be displayed from the Advanced settings dialog.

intent_routes.question: What are the bearing measurement options?
question_variations: How can I change bearing measurements?
What bearing formats are available?
Can I switch between true and magnetic bearings?
intent_routes.answer: Bearings can be measured in relation to True/Magnetic North (°T/°M) or relative to own vessel (°R). Note that True/Magnetic bearing requires a compass to be available.

intent_routes.question: How do I configure dangerous target settings?
question_variations: What defines a dangerous target?
How to set up dangerous vessel alerts?
Where are the collision warning settings?
intent_routes.answer: In the Vessels and Tracked Targets dialog, you can specify Time to closest point of approach and Closest point of approach to define when a vessel is considered dangerous.

intent_routes.question: What is the Safe Ring feature?
question_variations: How does the safe ring work?
Can I add a safety zone around my vessel?
What is the danger zone ring?
intent_routes.answer: Safe Ring adds a danger zone circle around your vessel. The radius equals the closest point of approach setting from the Vessels and Tracked Targets dialog.

intent_routes.question: How do I filter AIS targets?
question_variations: Can I limit the number of AIS targets shown?
How to hide slow moving vessels?
What are the AIS filtering options?
intent_routes.answer: Under Filtering settings, you can show all targets/dangerous targets/no targets, set maximum AIS targets displayed, hide targets slower than specified speed, and configure lost target hiding options.

intent_routes.question: How do I set the antenna position on my radar?
question_variations: Where do I enter radar antenna offset?
How do I configure antenna position settings?
What are the steps to set radar antenna location?
intent_routes.answer: Enter the X-axis and Y-axis offset distances in feet from the boat's center reference point. The PPI will be centered on the antenna position icon.

intent_routes.question: What height should I set for the radar antenna?
question_variations: How high should I set my radar antenna?
What's the correct antenna height setting?
Where do I enter antenna height?
intent_routes.answer: Enter the antenna height in meters measured from the waterline when vessel has typical load. This setting is crucial for proper sea clutter function.

intent_routes.question: What antenna span options are available?
question_variations: What antenna lengths can I choose from?
What are the available antenna span settings?
How do I set antenna span?
intent_routes.answer: You can choose between 4, 6, 9, or 12 ft antenna length options for the antenna span setting.

intent_routes.question: How do I search for AIS vessels?
question_variations: Where can I find nearby AIS targets?
What's the process to locate AIS vessels?
Can I search for specific AIS targets?
intent_routes.answer: Use the find option in the menu. With active cursor, it searches around cursor position. Without cursor, it searches around your vessel's position.

intent_routes.question: Where can I see all AIS vessel information?
question_variations: How do I view AIS target details?
Where is the list of AIS vessels?
How can I see AIS vessel data?
intent_routes.answer: Open the vessels dialog which shows a list of all targets sorted by distance to own vessel. It displays vessel name, distance, bearing, CPA, TCPA, type and status.

intent_routes.question: How do I view detailed AIS vessel information?
question_variations: Where can I find AIS vessel details?
How do I see more information about an AIS target?
What steps show AIS vessel details?
intent_routes.answer: To view AIS vessel details, select the AIS pop-up and then select the info option in the menu

intent_routes.question: What information is shown for AIS vessels on radar panels?
question_variations: What AIS data appears on radar displays?
What vessel details are shown on radar panels?
intent_routes.answer: Radar panels show vessel name, safety status, SOG (Speed Over Ground), COG (Course Over Ground), CPA (Closest Point of Approach), TCPA (Time to CPA), RNG (Range), and BRG (Bearing)
references: AIS information on radar panels section

intent_routes.question: How do I call an AIS vessel?
question_variations: What's needed to contact an AIS vessel?
Can I make DSC calls to AIS vessels?
intent_routes.answer: If you have a VHF radio supporting DSC calls over NMEA 2000® or NMEA 0183®, you can initiate DSC calls through the AIS vessel details dialog or vessel status dialog

intent_routes.question: What vessel details are shown in AIS information?
question_variations: What data is available about AIS vessels?
What information can I see about AIS targets?
intent_routes.answer: AIS details include MMSI, callsign, status, IMO number, navigation status, AIS class, draught, vessel type, position (lat/long), dimensions (length/beam), accuracy, rate of turn, bearing, speed, course, CPA/TCPA, heading, destination and ETA

intent_routes.question: What is DSC vessel tracking?
question_variations: How does DSC tracking work?
Can you explain DSC position tracking?
What is Digital Selective Calling for vessels?
intent_routes.answer: DSC (Digital Selective Calling) is a semi-automated method of requesting or receiving position data from vessels with DSC VHF radios. When received, it displays vessel icons on chart and radar panels with position coordinates, and may include COG and SOG data.

intent_routes.question: What happens when an AIS SART is activated?
question_variations: How does AIS SART work?
What occurs when a Search and Rescue Transponder activates?
How does the system respond to AIS SART signals?
intent_routes.answer: When activated, an AIS SART transmits position and identification data. On compliant AIS receivers, a red icon appears on the chart for 'Active' state or green for 'Test' state, and an alarm message is displayed with an optional audible alarm.

intent_routes.question: What information is shown in an AIS SART alarm message?
question_variations: What details are included in SART alerts?
What data appears in a SART alarm?
How can I read SART alarm information?
intent_routes.answer: AIS SART alarm messages display the SART's unique MMSI number, latitude, longitude, bearing in degrees, and distance from your vessel in miles.
references: Page 98, AIS SART Alarm Message Section

intent_routes.question: How do I respond to an AIS SART alarm?
question_variations: What are my options when receiving a SART alert?
What can I do when I get a SART alarm?
How to handle SART alarms?
intent_routes.answer: You have three options: 1) Ignore the alarm (mutes and closes message), 2) Save the waypoint (saves to waypoint list with MOB AIS SART prefix), or 3) Activate MOB function (switches to zoomed chart panel centered on SART position and creates active route).

intent_routes.question: How long does an AIS SART remain in the vessels list?
question_variations: When does a SART disappear from vessel tracking?
What's the SART tracking duration?
How long will I see SART signals?
intent_routes.answer: If the AIS stops receiving the AIS SART message, the SART remains in the vessels list for 10 minutes after receiving the last signal.

intent_routes.question: How do I activate the MOB AIS SART function?
question_variations: What is the process to activate MOB AIS SART?
How do I turn on MOB AIS SART tracking?
intent_routes.answer: When activated, the display switches to a zoomed chart panel centered on the AIS SART position and creates an active route to the AIS SART position. Note that if MOB function is already active, it will be terminated and replaced by the new route.

intent_routes.question: How long does an AIS SART remain in the vessels list after signal loss?
question_variations: What happens when AIS stops receiving SART messages?
When does an AIS SART disappear from the vessel list?
intent_routes.answer: The AIS SART remains in the vessels list for 10 minutes after receiving the last signal.

intent_routes.question: What are the options available when receiving a dangerous target alert?
question_variations: How do I respond to a dangerous target alert?
What can I do when I get a dangerous vessel warning?
intent_routes.answer: There are three options: 1) Disable - closes message and cancels alerts for all vessels, 2) Ignore - closes message and disables alert for that specific vessel only, 3) View - opens chart panel with the dangerous vessel's pop-up activated.

intent_routes.question: What happens when I select 'Disable' for dangerous target alerts?
question_variations: What does the Disable option do for dangerous target warnings?
How does disabling dangerous target alerts work?
intent_routes.answer: Selecting Disable turns off the Dangerous target alert option in the Alarms settings dialog. When disabled, dangerous target alert messages are not generated for either radar or AIS dangerous targets.

intent_routes.question: What colors are used for AIS dangerous target symbols?
question_variations: How are dangerous AIS targets colored on different radar palettes?
What color indicates a dangerous AIS target?
intent_routes.answer: Dangerous AIS targets are shown in yellow on black/red or black/green palettes, purple on white/red palette, and red on black/yellow palette.

intent_routes.question: What is an associated target in AIS?
question_variations: How does target association work?
What happens when radar and AIS detect the same target?
Can you explain associated targets?
intent_routes.answer: An associated target occurs when the radar and AIS signal acquire the same target. The system displays it as a single symbol to reduce clutter on the PPI. This function continues tracking AIS targets even if radar contact is lost, such as when behind an island.

intent_routes.question: How do I identify a lost AIS target?
question_variations: What indicates a lost AIS target?
How are lost targets displayed?
What symbol shows a lost AIS contact?
intent_routes.answer: A lost AIS target is indicated by a line through the target symbol. The symbol remains at the last known position received from the target.

intent_routes.question: What is MMSI and why do I need it?
question_variations: Why should I enter my MMSI number?
What's the purpose of MMSI?
Do I need to enter MMSI?
intent_routes.answer: MMSI (Maritime Mobile Service Identity) is required to receive addressed messages from AIS and DSC vessels. Entering your MMSI number also prevents your own vessel from appearing as an AIS target on your display.

intent_routes.question: What are extension lines?
question_variations: How do vessel extension lines work?
What do the course extension lines show?
What are COG and heading extension lines?
intent_routes.answer: Extension lines show the predicted course over ground and heading for your vessel and other vessels. The length indicates the distance the vessel will move in the selected time period. Your vessel uses heading sensor data and GPS COG information, while other vessels' data comes from AIS messages.

intent_routes.question: How are AIS SART icons displayed?
question_variations: What color are SART icons?
How do I identify AIS SART signals?
What's the difference between active and test SART icons?
intent_routes.answer: AIS SART 'active' icons are displayed in red, while AIS SART 'test' icons are shown in green.

intent_routes.question: How do I identify dangerous targets in AIS?
question_variations: What makes a target dangerous in AIS?
How are dangerous vessels defined?
intent_routes.answer: Dangerous targets are defined by two criteria: Time to closest point of approach (CPA) and Closest point of approach distance. You can specify both these values in the settings.

intent_routes.question: What is the range of interest for AIS targets?
question_variations: How far can I track AIS targets?
What's the tracking distance for vessels?
intent_routes.answer: Range of interest can be set to Auto (based on radar range if available) or a specific distance from your vessel. Targets beyond this range will be hidden.

intent_routes.question: How do I filter AIS targets?
question_variations: Can I limit the number of AIS targets shown?
How to reduce AIS target clutter?
intent_routes.answer: You can filter targets by showing all targets, dangerous targets only, or no targets. You can set a maximum number of AIS targets, hide slower targets below a specific speed, and hide lost targets after a specified time.

intent_routes.question: What does the echosounder show?
question_variations: What can I see with the echosounder?
What information does the sounder display?
intent_routes.answer: The echosounder shows the water and bottom beneath your vessel, displaying fish detection and sea floor structure. Key elements include surface, bottom, fish arches, range scale, depth, temperature, and frequency.

intent_routes.question: How do I zoom the echosounder image?
question_variations: Can I zoom in on the sounder display?
What's the process for zooming the sounder?
intent_routes.answer: You can zoom the image using the zoom bar. Drag the zoom bar up or down to view different parts of the water column. If the cursor is active, the system zooms in at the cursor position.

intent_routes.question: How do I start recording sonar log data?
question_variations: How to record sonar logs?
How do I begin logging sonar data?
What are the steps to record sonar?
intent_routes.answer: Select the record option in the recording dialog. You can save internally or to external storage. Specify filename, file format (sl3 for ForwardScan/StructureScan3D), save location, and bytes per sounding (3200). A flashing red symbol appears in top left when recording.

intent_routes.question: How do I stop recording sonar logs?
question_variations: How to end sonar recording?
What's the way to stop logging sonar?
How do I finish recording?
intent_routes.answer: Select the stop logging option in the recording dialog. The dialog shows filename, elapsed time, file size and other recording details before stopping.

intent_routes.question: How do I upload sonar logs to C-MAP Genesis?
question_variations: What's the process to upload to C-MAP Genesis?
How can I transfer sonar logs to Genesis?
Ways to send logs to C-MAP Genesis?
intent_routes.answer: Two methods: 1) Use services option and follow prompts to sign in and transfer files. 2) Use Storage dialog - select sonar logs icon, select logs to transfer, and follow sign-in prompts if needed. Transfers can be done later when internet connected.
references: Upload Sonar Logs to C-MAP Genesis section

intent_routes.question: Where can I view recorded sonar data?
question_variations: How do I access recorded sonar logs?
Where are my saved sonar recordings?
How to review saved sonar data?
intent_routes.answer: Select 'view sonar log' option in the echo settings dialog to review both internally and externally stored sounder records.

intent_routes.question: How do I set a custom depth range?
question_variations: How to manually set depth range?
Can I customize the depth range?
Setting upper and lower range limits?
intent_routes.answer: Select range menu option, then choose custom option. This allows manual setting of both upper and lower range limits. Note this puts system in manual range mode.

intent_routes.question: How do I set the range on the echosounder?
question_variations: What are the range settings?
How can I adjust the depth range?
How do I change sonar range?
intent_routes.answer: You can set the range in three ways: Auto range (8m default, system automatically displays from surface to bottom), Preset range levels (select manually from menu), or Custom range (manually set upper and lower limits)

intent_routes.question: What frequencies does the echosounder use?
question_variations: Which frequency should I use?
What's the difference between high and low frequency?
How do frequencies affect sonar performance?
intent_routes.answer: Low frequency (50 kHz) goes deeper with wider cone but more noise, good for bottom discrimination. High frequency (200 kHz) offers better target separation and less noise, better for high speeds

intent_routes.question: How do I adjust the gain settings?
question_variations: What does gain control do?
How to change sonar sensitivity?
Should I use auto or manual gain?
intent_routes.answer: Gain controls sensitivity - higher gain shows more details but adds clutter, lower gain might miss weak echoes. Available in manual or automatic mode, default is Auto

intent_routes.question: How do I measure distance between two points?
question_variations: Can I measure between two spots on the sonar?
What's the measuring tool process?
How to use cursor for measurements?
intent_routes.answer: 1. Position cursor on first point 2. Select measure menu option 3. Position cursor on second point 4. Distance appears in Cursor Information window. Continue adding points as needed

intent_routes.question: What is TVG and what does it do?
question_variations: How does Time Variable Gain work?
How can I reduce surface clutter?
What reduces wave action interference?
intent_routes.answer: TVG (Time Variable Gain) reduces surface clutter caused by wave action and boat wakes by decreasing receiver sensitivity near the surface

intent_routes.question: How do I use zoom mode on the sounder?
question_variations: How does zoom work on the echosounder?
What are zoom bars used for?
How do I magnify the sounder image?
intent_routes.answer: Zoom mode shows a magnified view on the left panel. Default zoom is 2x but can go up to 8x. Zoom bars on the right show the magnified range. Higher zoom reduces distance between bars. Move bars up/down to view different depths.

intent_routes.question: What is bottom lock mode?
question_variations: How does bottom lock work?
How can I view targets near the bottom?
intent_routes.answer: Bottom lock mode flattens the bottom on the left panel image, measuring from seabed (0) upwards. Bottom and zero line always show regardless of range scale. Useful for viewing targets close to the bottom.

intent_routes.question: What is the depth line feature?
question_variations: How do I show depth line?
What does the depth line do?
intent_routes.answer: The depth line is a line shown on the bottom surface when toggled on. It helps distinguish the bottom from fish and structures.

intent_routes.question: How do Fish ID symbols work?
question_variations: What are the Fish ID display options?
How can I show fish on the screen?
intent_routes.answer: Fish ID offers three display options: traditional fish arches, fish symbols, or fish symbols with depth indication. Can include beep notification. Note that not all fish symbols represent actual fish.

intent_routes.question: What is DownScan overlay?
question_variations: How do I use DownScan overlay?
Can I combine DownScan with regular sounder?
intent_routes.answer: DownScan overlay allows you to overlay DownScan images on regular Echosounder image when a DownScan capable transducer is connected. Activating overlay adds basic DownScan options to the menu.

intent_routes.question: How do I enable the internal echosounder channel?
question_variations: Where do I turn on the internal sonar?
How to activate internal echosounder?
intent_routes.answer: Select the internal echosounder channel option in settings to make it available for selection in the echosounder panel menu

intent_routes.question: What is network echosounder mode?
question_variations: How does network echosounder mode work?
Can I use multiple echosounder sources?
intent_routes.answer: Network echosounder mode determines if you can select single or multiple echosounder sources. Single source is automatic for legacy systems, while multi-source mode is for networks without legacy echosounders

intent_routes.question: How do I share transducers across the network?
question_variations: Can I share sonar with other units?
How to enable transducer sharing?
intent_routes.answer: Select 'Network Echosounder' option to share transducers with other units connected on the Ethernet network. This must be enabled to see other sonar devices on the network

intent_routes.question: What is structure depth offset?
question_variations: How do depth offsets work?
How to configure depth measurements?
intent_routes.answer: Structure depth offset adjusts depth readings based on transducer position. Negative offset shows depth from vessel bottom, positive offset shows depth from water surface, zero shows depth from transducer

intent_routes.question: How do I view sonar recordings?
question_variations: Where are saved sonar logs?
Can I replay sonar data?
intent_routes.answer: Use the 'View Sonar Log' function to view recordings. Logs display as paused images with scrolling control, cursor use, distance measurement and view options like live images

intent_routes.question: What is ForwardScan?
question_variations: How does ForwardScan work?
What does ForwardScan do?
intent_routes.answer: ForwardScan is a navigational aid that monitors the underwater environment ahead of your vessel during slow speed maneuvers. Requires a ForwardScan transducer installation

intent_routes.question: What is required to use ForwardScan?
question_variations: How do I enable ForwardScan?
What do I need for ForwardScan to work?
intent_routes.answer: A ForwardScan transducer must be mounted on your vessel to use the ForwardScan feature

intent_routes.question: What is the maximum forward range of ForwardScan?
question_variations: How far can ForwardScan see ahead?
What's the forward scanning distance limit?
intent_routes.answer: The maximum Forward range is 91 meters (300 feet)

intent_routes.question: How do I reduce interference on ForwardScan?
question_variations: What removes noise from ForwardScan?
How can I clear up the ForwardScan display?
intent_routes.answer: Use the Noise rejection filter to reduce signal interference and on-screen clutter

intent_routes.question: What do the warning zones show in ForwardScan?
question_variations: What are the colored zones in ForwardScan?
How are hazards marked in ForwardScan?
intent_routes.answer: Warning zones are displayed in yellow and critical zones are displayed in red on the screen

intent_routes.question: How do I pause the ForwardScan image?
question_variations: Can I freeze the ForwardScan display?
What stops the ForwardScan scanning?
intent_routes.answer: Select Pause from More options to stop the image and examine it in detail. Note that the system will not collect data while paused

intent_routes.question: What does the History ratio control?
question_variations: How do I show more sounder history?
What changes the wake display in ForwardScan?
intent_routes.answer: History ratio controls how much sounder history is shown behind the boat. A higher ratio shows more history

intent_routes.question: How do I record ForwardScan data?
question_variations: Can ForwardScan data be logged?
What format records ForwardScan?
intent_routes.answer: ForwardScan data can be recorded by selecting the sl3 file format in the record dialog

intent_routes.question: How do I record ForwardScan data?
question_variations: Can I log ForwardScan data?
What format do I use to record ForwardScan?
How to save ForwardScan logs?
intent_routes.answer: Select the sl3 file format in the record dialog to record ForwardScan log data

intent_routes.question: What are the critical ForwardScan installation settings?
question_variations: What settings do I need for ForwardScan installation?
How do I configure ForwardScan installation?
intent_routes.answer: Critical settings include: Critical forward range (30.0m), Critical depth (10.0m), Warning forward range (67.0m), Warning depth (15.0m), Transducer angle (+15 deg), Depth offset (+2.0m)

intent_routes.question: How do I adjust the transducer angle?
question_variations: What transducer angle should I use?
How to set ForwardScan transducer angle?
intent_routes.answer: Enter a positive value (0 to +15°) if transducer angles toward vessel front, or negative value (0 to -15°) if angled toward rear. Transducer should ideally be vertical to waterline. Use caution as large angle variations can distort depth data.

intent_routes.question: What is the depth offset setting used for?
question_variations: How does depth offset work?
Why set depth offset in ForwardScan?
intent_routes.answer: Depth offset adjusts depth readings to show either depth from lowest point of vessel (negative value) or depth from water surface (positive value). Set to 0 for depth below transducer only.

intent_routes.question: How do I enable ForwardScan critical zone alarms?
question_variations: Where do I turn on ForwardScan alarms?
How to activate depth warning alarms?
intent_routes.answer: Enable the Forward range alarm in the Alarm settings dialog to receive Critical Zone alarms when entering water shallow enough to cross critical zone thresholds

intent_routes.question: How many dashboards can I create in the instrument panel?
question_variations: What's the maximum number of dashboards allowed?
How many different dashboards can I set up?
intent_routes.answer: You can define up to ten dashboards within the instrument panel

intent_routes.question: How do I switch between different dashboards?
question_variations: What's the way to change dashboards?
Can I switch between dashboard views?
intent_routes.answer: You can switch between dashboards by either selecting the left and right arrow buttons on the panel or selecting the dashboard from the menu

intent_routes.question: What types of predefined dashboards are available?
question_variations: What dashboard styles come preset?
Which dashboard types are included by default?
intent_routes.answer: Predefined dashboard styles include vessel, navigation, angler and instrument information displays

intent_routes.question: How do I edit a dashboard?
question_variations: What's the process to modify a dashboard?
Can I customize dashboard gauges?
intent_routes.answer: To edit a dashboard: 1. Activate the menu 2. Select the edit option 3. Select the gauge you want to change 4. Select information to be displayed and configure limits 5. Save changes through the menu. Alternatively, press and hold on the gauge you want to change and select the information to be displayed

intent_routes.question: What weather information is available in the system?
question_variations: What weather data can I access?
How does the weather feature work?
intent_routes.answer: The system supports weather data in GRIB format available for download from various weather service suppliers and SIRIUS Marine Weather Service (North America only). Weather forecast data can be overlaid on the chart

intent_routes.question: How do I import GRIB weather files?
question_variations: Where can I import GRIB files from?
What are the ways to import GRIB data?
How do I load GRIB weather data?
intent_routes.answer: GRIB files can be imported in two ways: 1) From the storage manager directly, or 2) From the forecast menu option on the chart panel when Grib weather is set as the overlay

intent_routes.question: What happens to existing GRIB data when importing new files?
question_variations: Does importing GRIB data overwrite existing data?
Will I lose current GRIB data when importing?
intent_routes.answer: GRIB data that is imported overwrites the GRIB data currently in memory

intent_routes.question: How do I display GRIB weather on my chart?
question_variations: Can I overlay GRIB weather on my chart?
How do I show weather data on the chart panel?
intent_routes.answer: Select GRIB weather as an overlay option on your chart panel. This will expand the chart menu to show GRIB weather options where you can select weather symbols, set distance between barbs, and adjust symbol opacity

intent_routes.question: What information is shown in the GRIB information window?
question_variations: How do I read the GRIB information window?
What details are displayed in the GRIB window?
intent_routes.answer: The GRIB information window shows the date and time of the weather forecast, plus the selected forecast time in brackets. Negative values indicate historic weather data. When you select a position on the chart, it also shows weather details for that location

intent_routes.question: What weather display options are available?
question_variations: How can I customize the GRIB weather display?
What weather symbols can I show on the chart?
intent_routes.answer: Available display options include wind barbs, pressure contours, adjustable transparency, animation controls, and forecast options. You can also adjust the spacing between wind barbs and opacity of weather symbols

intent_routes.question: How do wind barbs indicate wind speed?
question_variations: What do wind barbs mean?
How do I read wind speed from barbs?
How are wind speeds shown with barbs?
intent_routes.answer: Wind speed is shown by combinations of barbs: small barb = 5 knots, large barb = 10 knots, arrow barb = 50 knots. Add barbs together for total speed (e.g. 3 large barbs + 1 small barb = 35 knots)

intent_routes.question: What does the wind barb direction indicate?
question_variations: How do I read wind direction from barbs?
Which way is the wind blowing on the barb?
intent_routes.answer: The tail of the wind barb shows the direction the wind is coming from. For example, if the tail points southeast, the wind is coming from the northwest.

intent_routes.question: How do I view weather details for a location?
question_variations: Can I see weather information for specific spots?
How to check weather details on the map?
intent_routes.answer: Select a weather icon when pop-up is enabled to display observation details. You can also access weather information from the menu by selecting the weather icon and choosing 'Info - Weather item' menu option.

intent_routes.question: Where is this weather service available?
question_variations: Which regions can access this weather service?
Is this weather service available worldwide?
intent_routes.answer: This weather service is only available in North America.

intent_routes.question: What is GRIB weather data?
question_variations: How does GRIB weather work?
What are GRIB files used for?
intent_routes.answer: GRIB files contain forecast information for multiple days and can be displayed as chart overlay. The data can be animated to show weather system development.

intent_routes.question: How do I import GRIB data?
question_variations: Where can I import GRIB files from?
Can I import weather GRIB data?
intent_routes.answer: GRIB data can be imported from any location visible in the storage manager. Note that importing new GRIB data will overwrite existing GRIB data in memory.

intent_routes.question: How do I animate GRIB weather forecasts?
question_variations: Can I animate weather data?
How to show weather forecast animation?
How do I view predicted weather over time?
intent_routes.answer: Select time and animation speed from the menu. The time shift is shown in brackets in the GRIB information window, relative to current GPS time. Animation length varies by file.

intent_routes.question: Where is SiriusXM weather available?
question_variations: Which regions can use SiriusXM weather?
Is SiriusXM weather available outside North America?
What's the coverage area for SiriusXM marine weather?
intent_routes.answer: SiriusXM weather is available for North America only, covering North American inland waters and coastal areas.

intent_routes.question: What do I need for SiriusXM weather access?
question_variations: How can I get SiriusXM weather on my system?
What's required for SiriusXM marine weather?
What equipment do I need for SiriusXM weather?
intent_routes.answer: You need a Navico WM-4 marine satellite weather receiver connected to your system and an appropriate SiriusXM subscription.

intent_routes.question: How can I check my Sirius signal strength?
question_variations: Where do I see Sirius signal quality?
What's my Sirius connection status?
How do I view Sirius signal level?
intent_routes.answer: Access the Sirius status panel when the weather module is connected. Signal strength is shown as 1/3 (weak), 2/3 (good) or 3/3 (preferred).

intent_routes.question: What information is shown on the weather overlay?
question_variations: What can I see on the weather chart overlay?
What weather data appears on charts?
What weather features are shown on the overlay?
intent_routes.answer: The weather overlay shows precipitation color shading, surface observations, storm icons, wind barbs, sea surface temperature (SST) color shading, and SST color bar.

intent_routes.question: How do I animate weather graphics?
question_variations: Can I play back weather data?
How does weather animation work?
How to view weather animation?
intent_routes.answer: You can animate weather in two ways: 1) With precipitation overlay for past conditions and immediate future 2) With colored wave height overlay for future predictions. Animation time is shown in the panel when active.

intent_routes.question: What weather alarms can I set?
question_variations: How do I set up weather alerts?
What weather alerts are available?
Can I get storm warnings?
intent_routes.answer: You can set alarms for lightning, storms, severe weather forecasts, and weather watchboxes. Lightning and storm alarms can be set for a specific range from your vessel. Weather watchbox alarms trigger when entering National Weather Service defined zones.

intent_routes.question: How do I set up the video panel?
question_variations: What are the video settings?
How do I configure video display?
What video options are available?
intent_routes.answer: Video panel setup includes selecting video source, video standard (AUTO), enabling cycling between sources (5-120 second intervals), adjusting brightness, and additional source-specific options. Settings are adjusted individually for each video source.

intent_routes.question: What is the audio controller?
question_variations: How does the audio system work?
What are the audio controls?
Where are the audio functions?
intent_routes.answer: The audio controller features control buttons, tools, and source-specific options. It includes a control bar, small/large displays, maximize button, source information, control buttons, and ON/OFF button. The OFF button is located in the source list on small displays.

intent_routes.question: Where do I find audio setup instructions?
question_variations: How do I install audio?
Where are audio installation details?
What documentation covers audio setup?
intent_routes.answer: Audio installation, setup and connection information can be found in the documentation included with the audio device. For display unit wire connection information, refer to the unit's installation manual.

intent_routes.question: What do the different precipitation colors mean on the weather display?
question_variations: How can I interpret the precipitation colors?
What do rain colors indicate on the map?
How is precipitation intensity shown?
intent_routes.answer: Rain is shown from light green (light rain) through yellow and orange to dark red (heavy rain). Snow is shown in blue. Mixed precipitation appears in pink. Darker colors indicate higher intensity.

intent_routes.question: How do I view sea surface temperature?
question_variations: Can I see water temperature on the display?
Where is the SST shown?
How is water temperature displayed?
intent_routes.answer: Sea Surface Temperature (SST) can be displayed either as color shading or as text. When using color coding, the SST color bar appears on the left side of the display. Color codes are customizable in the settings.

intent_routes.question: What do the wave height colors indicate?
question_variations: How can I interpret wave height colors?
What do the different wave colors mean?
How are wave heights shown on the display?
intent_routes.answer: Wave heights are shown using colors from blue (lowest waves) to dark red (highest waves). The color coding for wave heights can be customized in settings.

intent_routes.question: What surface features can be displayed?
question_variations: Which surface features are available?
What weather surface elements can I see?
Can I view fronts and pressure systems?
intent_routes.answer: Available surface features include fronts, isobars, and pressure points. Note that surface features cannot be displayed simultaneously with Wind.

intent_routes.question: How do I view cloud top information?
question_variations: Can I see cloud height data?
Where are cloud tops shown?
How is cloud height displayed?
intent_routes.answer: Cloud tops can be toggled on/off to show cloud height using a grey color palette, with darker greys indicating lower clouds. This feature requires certain SiriusXM subscriptions and cannot be shown simultaneously with Precipitation or Echo Tops.

intent_routes.question: What weather icons are available?
question_variations: Which weather symbols can I see?
What types of weather indicators are shown?
What weather markers are available?
intent_routes.answer: Available weather icons include tropical storm tracking, hurricane tracking (categories 1-5), tropical disturbance/depression tracking, storm attributes, lightning, watch box locations and warnings, and marine zone locations.

intent_routes.question: How do I adjust the color codes for temperature and waves?
question_variations: Can I customize the temperature color scale?
How do I change wave height colors?
Where do I modify SST color settings?
intent_routes.answer: You can define custom ranges for both SST and wave height color coding. For SST, set warm (27.9°C) and cool (4.0°C) thresholds. For waves, set maximum (3.0m) and minimum (0.0m) heights. Colors will scale automatically within these ranges.

intent_routes.question: How do I set up the audio server?
question_variations: Which device should be the audio server?
How to configure audio server settings?
intent_routes.answer: If multiple audio sources are connected to the network, you must select one device as the audio server. If only one device is present, it automatically becomes the default audio server.

intent_routes.question: What are the speaker zone controls?
question_variations: How do I adjust speaker settings?
What audio mixer options are available?
intent_routes.answer: Speaker zones can be controlled through the mixer with options for volume, balance, fade, center, sub level, low pass filter (85 Hz), bass, and treble adjustments. Volume adjustments to bass and treble affect all zones.

intent_routes.question: How do I select Sirius channels?
question_variations: What are the Sirius channel controls?
How to change Sirius stations?
intent_routes.answer: To select a Sirius channel, use the left or right audio control button. To page through favorite channels, use the up or down audio control button.

intent_routes.question: What video standards are supported?
question_variations: How do I set the video format?
What video formats work with the audio server?
intent_routes.answer: The video format can be set to PAL and must match the display connected to the Audio server. This setting is available under Options for SonicHub 2.

intent_routes.question: How does the internet connection work?
question_variations: What are the internet connectivity options?
How do I connect to the internet?
intent_routes.answer: The unit automatically connects to the internet when connected to an Ethernet network with internet access. Mobile/cell phone internet connections can also be used but may require large data usage.

intent_routes.question: How do I connect my MFD to the internet?
question_variations: How can I get internet on my display?
What are the ways to connect to internet?
intent_routes.answer: There are two ways to connect: 1) Connect directly to an Ethernet network with internet access for automatic connection, or 2) Use Wi-Fi by selecting Wireless settings and connecting to a Wi-Fi hotspot

intent_routes.question: How do I connect my phone to the MFD?
question_variations: Can I connect my tablet to the display?
How to pair mobile devices?
intent_routes.answer: Go to Wireless settings and select 'Connect your phone/tablet' option. This allows phones/tablets to connect for remote viewing and control of the unit.

intent_routes.question: Where are the Bluetooth settings?
question_variations: How do I access Bluetooth options?
Where can I find Bluetooth controls?
intent_routes.answer: Bluetooth settings can be found under Settings > Wireless. Select 'Bluetooth options' to open the Bluetooth dialog which lists enabled devices.

intent_routes.question: How do I enable Wi-Fi?
question_variations: Where is the Wi-Fi setting?
How to turn on wireless?
intent_routes.answer: Select 'Built-in Wi-Fi' under Wireless settings to enable/disable the internal Wi-Fi functionality. Note that disabling Wi-Fi reduces power consumption.

intent_routes.question: What are hotspot settings?
question_variations: How do I view hotspot details?
Where can I find my hotspot name?
intent_routes.answer: Hotspot settings display the MFD's network name (SSID) and key. This is only available when the MFD built-in hotspot is turned on.

intent_routes.question: How do I connect my phone to the MFD?
question_variations: How do I pair my phone with the MFD?
What are the steps to connect my phone?
How do I setup phone connectivity on MFD?
intent_routes.answer: Enable Bluetooth on your phone, then use the phone icon in the MFD toolbar to connect. Select your phone from the list of available devices and follow the pairing instructions on both the phone and MFD.

intent_routes.question: What phone features work with the MFD?
question_variations: What can I do with my phone connected to MFD?
Which phone functions are available on MFD?
intent_routes.answer: When connected, you can read and send text messages (except on iPhone) and view caller ID for incoming calls.

intent_routes.question: What are the iPhone limitations with MFD?
question_variations: How is iPhone different on MFD?
What can't I do with iPhone on MFD?
intent_routes.answer: iPhone has two main limitations: 1) Only incoming calls and messages received while connected are available, 2) Messages cannot be sent from the MFD due to iPhone not supporting message sending from Bluetooth devices.

intent_routes.question: How do I send a text message from the MFD?
question_variations: Can I send texts from MFD?
What's the process to send messages from MFD?
intent_routes.answer: Select the new message option in the message dialog to create a new text message. Note that this feature is not available for iPhone users.

intent_routes.question: Where can I see my phone notifications on MFD?
question_variations: How do I check messages on MFD?
Where are phone alerts shown on MFD?
intent_routes.answer: After connecting your phone, use the phone icon to display the list of messages and call history. Incoming messages and phone notifications will pop up on the MFD screen.

intent_routes.question: How do I connect my phone to the MFD display?
question_variations: How do I connect my tablet to the MFD?
What's the process to connect mobile devices to MFD?
How can I link my smartphone to the display unit?
intent_routes.answer: You can connect in two ways: 1) Connect both phone/tablet and MFD to the same Wi-Fi hotspot, or 2) Connect directly to the MFD acting as an access point by selecting the MFD's network name (SSID) in your device's Wi-Fi settings
references: Chapter 21 - Remote Control of the MFD

intent_routes.question: What can I do with the B&G mobile app?
question_variations: What features does the B&G app have?
What's possible with the B&G mobile application?
What functions are available in the B&G app?
intent_routes.answer: The B&G app allows you to: register your display unit, view/download documentation, create/sync waypoints/routes/tracks, explore POIs, monitor marine traffic and weather, mirror/control display unit, subscribe to Premium charts, and download/apply software updates
references: Chapter 21 - Remote Control of the MFD

intent_routes.question: Where can I download the B&G mobile app?
question_variations: How do I get the B&G app?
Which stores offer the B&G mobile app?
Where is the B&G app available?
intent_routes.answer: The B&G: Sailing & Navigation app can be downloaded from both the Apple App Store and Google Play stores
references: Chapter 21 - Remote Control of the MFD

intent_routes.question: What is Iperf used for?
question_variations: Why would I use Iperf?
What's the purpose of Iperf?
How does Iperf help with network testing?
intent_routes.answer: Iperf is a network performance tool used for testing wireless network performance around the vessel to identify weak spots or problem areas. It must be installed on a tablet device and requires the unit to run Iperf server before testing

intent_routes.question: What remote control options are available for the MFD?
question_variations: How can I remotely control my MFD?
What devices can control the MFD remotely?
What are the ways to control MFD from distance?
intent_routes.answer: Remote control options include: smartphones/tablets connected to same Wi-Fi hotspot as MFD, devices connected to MFD acting as Wi-Fi access point, and compatible remote control units connected to same NMEA network
references: Chapter 21 - Remote Control of the MFD

intent_routes.question: How do I connect my iPhone to the MFD?
question_variations: Why won't my iPhone connect to the MFD?
What do I do if iPhone connection fails?
intent_routes.answer: If connection fails, try these steps: 1) Reboot the MFD and restart the phone 2) Check the phone isn't connected to other Bluetooth devices 3) Manually set iPhone to allow notifications from the MFD

intent_routes.question: What should I do if notifications are delayed or missing?
question_variations: Why are my phone alerts delayed on MFD?
How do I fix delayed notifications?
intent_routes.answer: Change the connection profile from 'auto' to 'alternative' if you experience delayed alerts or no sound during calls

intent_routes.question: Why aren't text messages showing on my MFD?
question_variations: Text messages not appearing on MFD
How do I get texts to show on MFD?
intent_routes.answer: Check that the text app is not open and active on the iPhone

intent_routes.question: What is retail mode?
question_variations: How does retail mode work?
What happens in retail mode?
intent_routes.answer: Retail mode shows a regional demonstration for showroom display. It pauses when operated and resumes after a timeout period

intent_routes.question: How do I manage message settings?
question_variations: Where can I change message templates?
How do I set up message alerts?
intent_routes.answer: Message settings can be configured in the settings dialog where you can define message templates and set alert types like popup and audio alerts

intent_routes.question: What is retail mode used for?
question_variations: What's the purpose of retail mode?
Why would I use retail mode?
intent_routes.answer: Retail mode is designed specifically for retail and showroom demonstrations of the device

intent_routes.question: How do I access the simulator source files?
question_variations: Where can I find simulator files?
What simulator data files can I use?
intent_routes.answer: You can select from pre-recorded data files included in your device, your own recorded log files, or log files on a connected mass storage device. Available file types include radar.rsf, sonarmiami2.sl2, ais.rsf, and riley.wx for weather

intent_routes.question: How do I control the simulator settings?
question_variations: What simulator settings can I adjust?
How do I change simulator parameters?
intent_routes.answer: Use Advanced simulator settings to manually control GPS source, simulated course, speed, course heading, route selection and start position

intent_routes.question: Where do I find the toolbar?
question_variations: How do I access the toolbar?
Where is the toolbar located?
intent_routes.answer: The toolbar is displayed on the home page. Press the Pages/Home key to display the home page and scroll to view toolbar options

intent_routes.question: What information does the Trip Calculator show?
question_variations: What can I see in the Trip Calculator?
What data is in the Trip Calculator?
intent_routes.answer: The Trip Calculator displays voyage and engine information with reset options, Race Timer controls, and three trip logs: Today (calendar date data), Trip 1, and Trip 2 accumulation data

intent_routes.question: How do trip logs work?
question_variations: When do trip logs record data?
What triggers trip logging?
intent_routes.answer: Trip logging occurs when enabled and while the vessel exceeds the threshold speed set for that specific trip panel (Today, Trip 1, or Trip 2)

intent_routes.question: What vessel information can I view?
question_variations: What boat data can I see?
What vessel details are available?
intent_routes.answer: The Vessels status list displays status and available information for AIS and DSC vessel types

intent_routes.question: How do I reset the trip distance?
question_variations: How can I zero out the trip distance?
Where is the reset for distance traveled?
How do I clear the trip meter?
intent_routes.answer: Select Reset from the Tools menu, then choose 'Distance' to reset Trip distance and DSTWR to 0, or select 'All' to reset all trip values including distance.

intent_routes.question: What time will the sun rise today?
question_variations: How do I check sunrise time?
Where can I find sun and moon information?
How do I see sunset times?
intent_routes.answer: Use the Sun, Moon tool to view sunrise, sunset, moonrise and moonset times based on your position's latitude/longitude and entered date.

intent_routes.question: How do I change the system language?
question_variations: Where are language settings?
Can I switch the display language?
How do I set the language?
intent_routes.answer: Go to System Settings and select Language to change the language used on the unit.

intent_routes.question: What is the PIN code used for?
question_variations: Why do I need a PIN code?
What features are protected by PIN?
When is the PIN required?
intent_routes.answer: The PIN code prevents unauthorized access to settings, alarms, storage and store features. Once entered, all protected features can be accessed without re-entering the PIN until the system is restarted.

intent_routes.question: How do I connect my phone to the MFD?
question_variations: Can I pair my phone with the display?
Where is the phone connection setting?
How do I sync my phone?
